guideTitle: Best GE Profile Opal Ice Makers (2026)
metaTitle: Best GE Profile Opal Ice Makers (2026)
metaDescription: Five GE Profile Opal nugget ice makers compared: Opal 2.0 Ultra, the scale-filter version, the Mini and Mini Pro, and the XL side-tank Ultra for heavy use.
expertTake: The GE Profile Opal 2.0 Ultra with the scale inhibiting filter is the pick for hard-water homes, since the filter attacks the main enemy of a nugget machine. The Opal Mini is the one for small kitchens that want ice in about five minutes. Skip the XL side-tank Ultra unless you truly host often, because the extra water capacity is a convenience you can live without.
introParagraphs: Opal is the line that taught many households what nugget ice is. The soft, chewable pellets come from an auger that scrapes a frozen cylinder and presses the shavings together, and the machines that make them are tall, heavy and rather loud compared with a bullet maker. People buy them for the ice, and they live with the rest.

Within the line the differences are about size, water capacity, speed and how much help the machine gives with scale. We compare each model on those points, on the cleaning it asks for and on who should pay the extra for the larger or smarter versions.

products.name: GE Profile Opal 2.0 Ultra nugget ice maker with scale inhibiting filter, 38 lb
products.description:
Scale is what kills nugget machines, and this Opal 2.0 Ultra includes a scale inhibiting filter aimed squarely at it. The filter sits in the water path and helps keep minerals from coating the evaporator, which stretches the interval between descales and protects the auger. For a hard-water home that is the most useful feature in the whole line.

It also carries the TrueFill ice system, which keeps the supply topped up so you stop checking the bin, and an advanced cleaning system that helps sanitize the machine without scrubbing. The output is 38 pounds a day of chewable pellets. A scoop comes in the box.

Compared with the Opal 2.0 Ultra with the 0.75 gallon tank it adds the filter and cleaning system as headline items. Replace the filter on the maker's schedule, descale periodically and keep vent clearance.
products.bestFor: Hard-water homes that want the best defense against scale.
pros: Scale inhibiting filter protects the evaporator
TrueFill keeps the bin topped up
Advanced cleaning system helps sanitize
38 lb per day with a scoop included
cons: Large, heavy and louder than a bullet maker

products.name: GE Profile Opal 2.0 Ultra nugget ice maker, 0.75 gal tank, WiFi, 38 lb
products.description:
The Opal 2.0 Ultra with the 0.75 gallon tank is the core of the current line. It delivers a first batch in about ten minutes or less and makes about 1.6 pounds of ice per hour, which works out to the 38 pounds a day rating. WiFi lets you start it from your phone.

The expanded tank is the upgrade over earlier Opals, making roughly three times as much ice at a time between refills and reducing trips to the sink. The Opal pellets are the soft, chewable type that people copy and rarely match.

Against the version with the scale filter it lacks that protection, so hard water is more of a worry. Descale monthly, wipe the bin and keep clearance around the vents, and use filtered water if your tap is hard.
products.bestFor: Households that want a smart, mid-size Opal with a big tank.
pros: First batch in about 10 minutes or less
About 1.6 lb per hour steady rate
0.75 gallon tank means fewer refills
WiFi start and scheduling
cons: No scale filter in this version
Needs more descaling in hard water

products.name: GE Profile Opal Mini nugget ice maker, 36 lb, 5 minute ice, top fill
products.description:
The Mini shrinks the Opal into a smaller body and speeds up the first batch to about five minutes or less, with up to 36 pounds a day. A top-fill station lets you pour water in from above without sliding the machine around, which matters in a small kitchen where the Opal sits under a cabinet.

The maker points out that the ice stays flavorful and does not water down your drink as fast as some others. The trade for the small body is a smaller reservoir, so you refill more often than on the Ultra. It makes slightly less than the 38 pound models.

Against the Ultra it is smaller and quicker to start with a smaller tank. Descale on schedule, keep clearance around the vents and clean the bin regularly.
products.bestFor: Small kitchens that want a quick-start nugget machine.
pros: First ice in 5 minutes or less
Top-fill reservoir is easy to refill
Smaller body for tight counters
Up to 36 lb per day
cons: Slightly lower output than the Ultra

products.name: GE Profile Opal Mini Pro nugget ice maker with side tank, 36 lb, top fill
products.description:
The Mini Pro adds a side tank to the Mini's compact body, which answers the Mini's main complaint: too many refills. Water capacity grows, the first batch still arrives in about five minutes or less, and the output stays at up to 36 pounds a day.

The top-fill station remains for quick pours. A side tank widens the footprint a little, so the compact idea is partly traded back. It is the pick for a household that wants the Mini's speed with more water between refills.

Compared with the Mini it holds more water, and compared with the Ultra it is smaller and lighter on output. Clean the side tank regularly so the water does not go stale, descale monthly and keep the vents clear.
products.bestFor: Households that want Mini speed with fewer refills.
pros: Side tank reduces refills

Top-fill station remains
Portable countertop body
cons: Side tank water can go stale if left

products.name: GE Profile Opal Ultra nugget ice maker, 1 gal XL side tank, 38 lb
products.description:
The XL side tank is the point: a one gallon reservoir that the maker says can make up to three times more ice from a fill, paired with 38 pounds a day and a removable three pound storage bin. For a family that entertains, it means fewer trips to the sink and a bigger reserve in the bin.

The first batch takes about ten minutes, and WiFi lets you start it remotely. The extra size is real: this is the largest Opal in the guide, and it takes counter space and some effort to move. The ice is the same original soft chewable pellet as in the smaller models.

Compared with the 0.75 gallon Ultra it adds more water capacity and a bigger bin. Clean the side tank on a schedule, descale in hard water and keep vent clearance.
products.bestFor: Large families and frequent hosts that want the most reserve.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Opal 2.0 Ultra's 0.75 gallon tank makes roughly three times more ice per fill than earlier models, the Ultra with the 1 gallon XL side tank goes further, and the Mini has the smallest reservoir. A larger tank means fewer trips to the sink and less downtime during a party. Count how often you will refill before choosing size. A household that makes ice mostly in the morning and evening can live with the Mini's small tank, while one that runs the machine all afternoon will tire of it quickly.

Hard water is the main enemy of a nugget machine because scale coats the cylinder and slows the auger. The Opal 2.0 Ultra with the scale inhibiting filter attacks it directly, while the others rely on descaling. If your water is hard, the filter is worth more than any other feature. A cheap hardness test strip tells you where you stand, and a household whose water leaves white crust on a kettle should treat scale protection as a requirement, not an option.

The Mini and Mini Pro claim a first batch in 5 minutes or less, while the Ultra models claim 10 minutes or less. After the first batch the steady rate is about 1.6 pounds an hour on the Ultra. A fast start suits impulse drinks, but the steady rate decides how fast the bin fills.

The Mini fits under a cabinet and a small counter, while the XL side-tank Ultra needs real space. A side tank widens the footprint. Measure your counter, the height under the cabinet and the room for the side tank before ordering. Also check where you will pour water in, since a top-fill station needs headroom above the machine and a side tank needs room beside it.

The Opal 2.0 Ultra with the scale filter lists an advanced cleaning system that helps sanitize the machine without scrubbing. It does not replace a periodic descale, but it slows biofilm and reduces the work. For a machine you run daily, a good cleaning routine is part of the price.

WiFi on the Ultra models lets you start the machine from your phone. Every Opal is louder than a bullet maker because of the auger and compressor, so place it away from a bedroom wall. Smart features are conveniences, so confirm that the machine runs from its own panel if the app fails.

howWeEvaluated.description: We rewarded the scale inhibiting filter on the Opal 2.0 Ultra and noted that the other models rely on descaling. In a hard-water home this is the biggest durability factor. Filters are a recurring cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water capacity

howWeEvaluated.description: We compared first-ice claims of 5 and 10 minutes and the steady 1.6 pounds an hour. A fast start scored for impulse use. The steady rate decides bin refill.

cards.label: Mini and Mini Pro
cards.text: These are smaller, start in about 5 minutes and make up to 36 lb a day. The Mini Pro adds a side tank.

cards.label: Ultra
cards.text: The Ultra models make up to 38 lb a day, start in about 10 minutes and add WiFi, bigger tanks and more storage.

howToChoose.note: Mini for small counters and quick starts; Ultra for families and big tanks. Neither is quiet, so the choice rarely turns on sound, and it usually comes down to counter space and how often you can stand to refill.

cards.text: A scale inhibiting filter, a descale routine and filtered water. Check the water hardness before buying.

maintenance.why: A spent filter stops protecting the evaporator. Mark the date on a calendar, and replace the filter earlier than scheduled if your water is very hard or the machine runs all day.
Scale slows the auger. The interval is longer with the filter and shorter without it, and a machine that is run daily in hard water may need descaling monthly even with a filter in place.
Water sitting in a large tank goes stale and grows film. Rinse and refill with fresh water.
A damp bin grows biofilm. A soft cloth and a mild cleaner keep it fresh, and the area around the chute is the first spot where residue collects, so check it whenever you take out the storage bin.

An Opal that sits in a dusty corner loses cooling airflow, which raises the hum and trims ice production. A soft brush on the grille and a few inches of open space on every side keep the compressor cool, and an Opal tucked into a corner is the one most likely to run hot.

faq.q: What makes the Opal different from other nugget ice makers?
faq.a: It is the original soft chewable nugget machine, and the maker positions its ice as the one that cannot be imitated. The practical differences are tank size, speed, scale protection and brand support. Nugget ice from any auger machine is made the same basic way, so the Opal's edge is more about how well the whole package is engineered and supported than about a unique kind of ice.

faq.q: Which Opal is best for hard water?
faq.a: The Opal 2.0 Ultra with the scale inhibiting filter. The filter reduces mineral buildup on the evaporator, which stretches the time between descales. Replace the cartridge on the maker's schedule, because a spent filter gives no protection, and keep a spare so a replacement never leaves the machine unguarded.

faq.q: How much ice does an Opal make per hour?
faq.a: About 1.6 pounds an hour on the Opal 2.0 Ultra, which works out to the 38 pound daily rating. The first batch takes about 10 minutes or less on the Ultra and 5 on the Mini. Those rates are claims for a cool room and cold water, and a warm kitchen will trim them, so the first batch is better thought of as a starting gun than a guarantee.

faq.q: Do I need the side tank?
faq.a: Only if you refill often or entertain. A side tank cuts trips to the sink and makes more ice per fill, but it widens the machine and needs cleaning. A side tank that is topped off with fresh water every week stays clean, while one that sits for a month with a film on the walls will flavor the ice.

Louder than a bullet maker, because of the auger and compressor. Place the machine away from a bedroom and leave vent clearance. Owners often describe the auger sound as a steady grind that fades into the background of a busy kitchen, but it is not a machine for a bedside table or a quiet home office.

faq.q: Does the storage bin keep ice frozen?
faq.a: No. The bin is not a freezer, so melt water drains back to the reservoir. Use the ice fresh or bag and freeze it. A removable storage bin like the XL Ultra's three pound one helps you grab a batch, but a freezer bag with the air pressed out is the real way to keep a surplus for the weekend.
